children: lost nearly 40% in the premarket on Tuesday after the cancer drug developer said that the U.S. FDA has recommended it to run an additional trial before submitting a marketing application for its lead asset, tovecimig.

The Boston, Massachusetts-based biotech is looking to submit a Biologics License Application for the bispecific antibody later this year, targeting patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer based on its Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 study.
Citing feedback from a recent meeting with the regulator, Compass
said that the FDA recommended it to conduct a trial to show the survival benefit of tovecimig, a decision it doesn’t agree with.

“Compass does not believe that a new trial is warranted prior to submitting a BLA based on the data from the Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 study and the urgent unmet medical need for patients with BTC,” the company said.

While COMPANION-002 reached the primary endpoint of objective response rate, indicating a statistically significant improvement versus paclitaxel, its overall survival data fell short of statistical significance.
said it will continue to engage with the FDA as it readies a BLA

title: Compass Therapeutics drops as FDA seeks additional trial for lead asset
